etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English ounce, unce, from Middle French once, from Latin uncia (“Roman ounce, various similar units”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *óynos (“one”). Doublet of a, one, inch, uncia, onça, onza, oka, ouguiya, and awqiyyah.

definitions.definition: An avoirdupois ounce, weighing 1⁄16 of an avoirdupois pound, or 28.349523125 grams.
A troy ounce, weighing 1⁄12 of a troy pound, or 480 grains, or 31.1034768 grams.
A US fluid ounce, with a volume of 1⁄16 of a US pint, 1.804688 cubic inches or 29.5735295625  millilitres.
A British imperial fluid ounce, with a volume of 1⁄20 of an imperial pint, 1.733871 cubic inches or 28.4130625 millilitres.
(figurative) Any small amount, a little bit.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French once, from Old French lonce (“lynx”), by false division (the l was thought to be the article), from Italian lonza, ultimately from Ancient Greek λύγξ (lúnx, “lynx”). Doublet of onza and lynx.

definitions.definition: (archaic) A large wild feline, such as a lynx or cougar. [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 1634, William Wood, “Of the Beasts that Live on the Land”, in New Englands Prospect. A True, Lively, and Experimentall Description of that Part of America, Commonly Called New England; […], London:  […]  Tho[mas] Cotes, for Iohn Bellamie, […], →OCLC, 1st part, page 23:
quote.text: The Ounce or the vvilde Cat, is as big as a mungrell dog, this creature is by nature feirce, and more dangerous to bee met vvithall than any other creature, not fearing eyther dogge or man;  […]

quote.citation: 1801, Robert Southey, “(please specify the page)”, in Thalaba the Destroyer, volume (please specify |volume=I or II), London:  […]  [F]or T[homas] N[orton] Longman and O[wen] Rees, […], by Biggs and Cottle, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Halloa! another prey,The nimble Antelope!The ounce is freed; one spring,And his talons are sheath’d in her shoulders,And his teeth are red in her gore.

definitions.definition: Synonym of snow leopard, Panthera uncia. [from 18th c.]
(cryptozoology) Synonym of onza, a particularly aggressive cougar or jaguarundi in Mexican folklore.

quote.citation: 1911, James George Frazer, The Golden Bough, volume 8, page 235:
quote.text: The ounce, a leopard-like creature, is dreaded for its depredations by the Indians of Brazil.
